input:
Create a Splunk detection rule for MITRE ATT&CK T1059.001 (PowerShell).
Behavior to detect: Detects PowerShell started with an encoded command parameter, a common way to hide malicious scripts.
Available data source: Sysmon EventID 1

output.title: PowerShell Execution With Encoded Command
output.description: Detects PowerShell started with an encoded command parameter, a common way to hide malicious scripts.
output.sigma_rule:
title: PowerShell Execution With Encoded Command
id: 2ee55d77-41c8-5f66-92d6-3a3bf21106f9
status: experimental
description: Detects PowerShell started with an encoded command parameter.
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_cli:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -enc '
      - ' -encodedcommand '
      - ' -e '
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Administrative or deployment scripts that use encoded commands
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.001
output.spl_query: sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 (Image="*\\powershell.exe" OR Image="*\\pwsh.exe") (CommandLine="* -enc *" OR CommandLine="* -encodedcommand *" OR CommandLine="* -e *") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by host User ParentImage Image CommandLine
false_positives: Software deployment tools (SCCM, Intune) that launch encoded PowerShell
Administrative scripts written by IT staff
response_actions: Decode the Base64 command line and review what it executes.
Check the parent process and the user account that launched PowerShell.
Search for network connections and file writes from the same process.
Isolate the host if the decoded script is malicious.
output.how_to_implement: Ingest Sysmon Operational logs (Splunk Add-on for Sysmon) with process creation (EventID 1) enabled.

input:
Create a Splunk detection rule for MITRE ATT&CK T1003.001 (LSASS Memory).
Behavior to detect: Detects processes opening a handle to lsass.exe with memory-read access rights, which indicates credential dumping tools such as Mimikatz.
Available data source: Sysmon EventID 10

output.title: LSASS Memory Access by Uncommon Process
output.description: Detects processes opening a handle to lsass.exe with memory-read access rights, which indicates credential dumping tools such as Mimikatz.
output.sigma_rule:
title: LSASS Memory Access by Uncommon Process
id: 53d54ca4-0d9d-541d-be51-981cc7d9096b
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious access to LSASS process memory.
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_access
detection:
  selection:
    TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    GrantedAccess|contains:
      - '0x1010'
      - '0x1410'
      - '0x1fffff'
  filter_legit:
    SourceImage|endswith:
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\wmiprvse.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Endpoint security and backup software
level: critical
tags:
  - attack.credential-access
  - attack.t1003.001
output.spl_query: sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=10 TargetImage="*\\lsass.exe" (GrantedAccess="0x1010" OR GrantedAccess="0x1410" OR GrantedAccess="0x1fffff") NOT (SourceImage="*\\MsMpEng.exe" OR SourceImage="*\\wmiprvse.exe") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by host SourceImage SourceUser GrantedAccess
false_positives: EDR, antivirus and backup agents that legitimately read LSASS memory
response_actions: Identify the source process and verify whether it is a known security tool.
Collect the binary and memory dump for analysis.
Reset credentials of accounts that logged on to the host.
Isolate the host and hunt for lateral movement with the same credentials.
output.how_to_implement: Ingest Sysmon logs with ProcessAccess (EventID 10) enabled for lsass.exe.

input:
Create a Splunk detection rule for MITRE ATT&CK T1053.005 (Scheduled Task).
Behavior to detect: Detects schtasks.exe creating a task that runs a program from user-writable folders such as AppData, Temp or Public.
Available data source: Sysmon EventID 1

output.title: Scheduled Task Created via Schtasks From Suspicious Location
output.description: Detects schtasks.exe creating a task that runs a program from user-writable folders such as AppData, Temp or Public.
output.sigma_rule:
title: Scheduled Task Created From Suspicious Location
id: 33958017-7287-52fa-8af9-6c78b06ad7e9
status: experimental
description: Detects schtasks creating tasks that run from user-writable paths.
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/create'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
  condition: selection and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Software installers that register update tasks
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1053.005
output.spl_query: sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 Image="*\\schtasks.exe" CommandLine="*/create*" (CommandLine="*\\AppData\\*" OR CommandLine="*\\Temp\\*" OR CommandLine="*\\Users\\Public\\*") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by host User ParentImage CommandLine
false_positives: Legitimate application updaters that install into AppData (browsers, chat clients)
response_actions: Review the task name, schedule and the program it runs.
Check the program's hash and signature.
Delete the task and quarantine the file if malicious.
Look for other persistence created at the same time.
output.how_to_implement: Ingest Sysmon Operational logs (Splunk Add-on for Sysmon) with process creation (EventID 1) enabled.

input:
Create a Splunk detection rule for MITRE ATT&CK T1547.001 (Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder).
Behavior to detect: Detects script interpreters or LOLBins writing to Run or RunOnce registry keys to establish persistence.
Available data source: Sysmon EventID 13

output.title: Registry Run Key Modified by Script Interpreter
output.description: Detects script interpreters or LOLBins writing to Run or RunOnce registry keys to establish persistence.
output.sigma_rule:
title: Registry Run Key Modified by Script Interpreter
id: edf180a4-1bf4-5801-a984-be6e8a547f4c
status: experimental
description: Detects interpreters adding Run key persistence.
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: registry_set
detection:
  selection_key:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\CurrentVersion\Run\'
      - '\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\'
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\reg.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Login scripts managed by IT
level: high
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1547.001
output.spl_query: sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=13 (TargetObject="*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\*" OR TargetObject="*\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\*") (Image="*\\powershell.exe" OR Image="*\\cmd.exe" OR Image="*\\wscript.exe" OR Image="*\\mshta.exe" OR Image="*\\reg.exe") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by host User Image TargetObject Details
false_positives: IT-managed login scripts that register startup items with reg.exe
response_actions: Inspect the registry value and the file it points to.
Remove the Run key entry and quarantine the file if malicious.
Identify how the interpreter was launched (parent process, user).
output.how_to_implement: Ingest Sysmon logs with RegistryEvent (EventID 13) enabled for Run keys.

input:
Create a Splunk detection rule for MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011 (Rundll32).
Behavior to detect: Detects rundll32.exe with command lines that execute JavaScript, load DLLs from user folders or UNC paths.
Available data source: Sysmon EventID 1

output.title: Rundll32 Executing Script or Remote Code
output.description: Detects rundll32.exe with command lines that execute JavaScript, load DLLs from user folders or UNC paths.
output.sigma_rule:
title: Rundll32 Executing Script or Remote Code
id: b1e865d2-8e21-5304-9c4a-6dcdd103827f
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious rundll32 command lines.
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_cli:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'javascript:'
      - '\\'
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Temp\'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legacy software loading DLLs from temporary folders
level: high
tags:
  - attack.defense-evasion
  - attack.t1218.011
output.spl_query: sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 Image="*\\rundll32.exe" (CommandLine="*javascript:*" OR CommandLine="*\\\\*" OR CommandLine="*\\AppData\\*" OR CommandLine="*\\Temp\\*") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by host User ParentImage CommandLine
false_positives: Legacy installers that load DLLs from Temp
response_actions: Retrieve the DLL referenced in the command line and check its hash.
Review the parent process chain.
Block the DLL hash and isolate the host if malicious.
output.how_to_implement: Ingest Sysmon Operational logs (Splunk Add-on for Sysmon) with process creation (EventID 1) enabled.

input:
Create a Splunk detection rule for MITRE ATT&CK T1110.001 (Password Guessing).
Behavior to detect: Detects more than 10 failed logons for the same account from one source within 10 minutes, indicating password guessing.
Available data source: Windows Security EventID 4625

output.title: Multiple Failed Logons for a Single Account
output.description: Detects more than 10 failed logons for the same account from one source within 10 minutes, indicating password guessing.
output.sigma_rule:
title: Multiple Failed Logons for a Single Account
id: f1cea17f-c043-53a0-b4c0-d3c1116d4d92
status: experimental
description: Detects password guessing via repeated failed logons.
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4625
  filter_machine:
    TargetUserName|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection and not filter_machine
falsepositives:
  - Users with expired passwords
  - Misconfigured services using old credentials
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.credential-access
  - attack.t1110.001
output.spl_query: sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4625 | bin _time span=10m | stats count dc(host) as hosts values(host) as hosts_list by _time TargetUserName IpAddress | where count > 10
false_positives: Users repeatedly mistyping after a password change
response_actions: Check whether any successful logon (4624) followed from the same source.
Contact the account owner to confirm activity.
Block the source IP if external and lock the account if compromised.
Enforce MFA for the account.
output.how_to_implement: Ingest Windows Security logs from domain controllers and servers with logon auditing enabled.
